Interactive demo of the Aether app, with three selectable stories. Start an agent: the new-task composer types a prompt, a devbox boots in about five seconds with a live terminal, file tree, and a shareable preview link on port 3000, and the agent fixes a broken mobile order summary, captures before-and-after screenshots and a session video into the thread, asks one question, and opens pull request #1851 with a preview link and passing checks. The review loop: aether review requests changes on a pull request, the agent folds both fixes in, and the re-review approves. PR review: the reviewer surface at /pr-reviews streams three inline findings onto a pull request and posts a changes-requested verdict. Buttons inside the demo switch tasks and pages and answer the question; the pause control freezes all motion.

Oversight

A loop you can watch and take over.

Every command and diff streams as it lands — watch the whole run, or step in and take over at any point.

  • Plan mode: the agent proposes, you approve, then it executes
  • Queue follow-ups mid-run and the agent folds them in without restarting
  • Stop the agent anytime and the devbox stays alive, yours to use

Demo: an agent streams commands and diffs into the task thread while a typed follow-up queues without interrupting it; in a separate pane, the human runs npm test in their own terminal and the suite passes.

FAQ

Questions

Encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM under a key derived per user, and injected into your isolated VM only for the duration of a session. You can revoke them at any time. The security page describes the full picture.

Each task gets its own Firecracker microVM that is never reused for another task or another user. The devbox suspends when idle, and the machine and its volume are destroyed when your pull request merges or closes, or after 48 hours of inactivity. The devbox is open the whole time, so you can watch every command your agent runs.

No. And because the agent runs on your own provider account, what your model provider does with your code is governed by your account and its settings; we're not in that loop.

Aether reviews pull requests in repositories where you install the GitHub App. Pull requests from forks run in review only mode.

Credits meter active runtime only, per second. One credit is twelve minutes on the default Small devbox; Medium runs at 2× and Large at 4×. Idle and suspended devboxes bill nothing, and warm slots are a plan entitlement that never consumes credits.

Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode, each running on your own provider account, whether that is a subscription or an API key. Across the three you can reach 40+ models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and more, and you can set the model and reasoning effort per task.

Yes. A documented REST API with platform keys covers projects, tasks, automations, and usage, and a WebSocket API streams the live workspace: terminal, files, agent events, ports, and git. The CLI is built on the same surface.

Yes: self-serve via the billing portal, effective at the end of your billing cycle. The Free plan is permanent, so you can also just step down to it.
